approved_or_rejected_by: L1.deletion-withdraws approved 2026-09-17; this document proposed, awaiting the L2 recompile it demands

blocked_on.L1.constructed-scenarios: The D-only trade case. Claiming a D-only trade absent requires a scenario naming a trade number the records do not carry, which the clause's second sentence forbids a constructed scenario from introducing. The pair (372101, 353232) in this document is a holding, not a trade, so it is admissible; a D-only trade is not.
blocked_on.L1.hole.change-effective-time: The account and customer halves. ownership-history's CDC handoffs are deferred under this hole, so the job does not read the sources that carry the flag. Answering L1.hole.deletions did not make the account case testable; it made visible that the case sits behind a second open hole.
blocked_on.inv.customer_withdrawal_with_standing_ac: Why the row-producing case is not in this document rather than merely absent from it. A customer withdrawal can only reach ownership-history through raw.customer_cdc, whose handoffs are all deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time, so the job does not read it. The one labeled source it does read, ce.account_changes, is anchored with the fields account_id, action_at, tax_status_id, status_id and provenance -- there is no field on it that can mark a row as a withdrawal, and none that names a customer. So L1.constructed-scenarios' new withdrawal exception is correctly stated and, for this job, currently unexercisable: the exception permits a scenario the anchored constructed source has no way to express. Making it exercisable is a shape change to the anchors, which is not this document's to propose. Recorded here so that the invariant's missing counterexample is a known, explained absence rather than an oversight.

deterministic_assertion: On both engines, with this scenario loaded: account 624 has no current statement and no as-of answer at or after 2017-07-08; its 2008-03-14 and 2010-02-07 statements and every as-of answer before 2017-07-08 match a run without the scenario; no holding_change exists for the pair (372101, 353232); and account 428's statements, trades and holding changes are byte-identical to a run without the scenario. Every must-hold audit is at zero and the two engines agree.

expected.account_624: Its 2008-03-14 and 2010-02-07 statements stand with their standing facts byte-identical to a run without this scenario. 624 has no current statement. An as-of question at any moment before 2017-07-08 answers exactly as it did without the scenario; an as-of question at or after 2017-07-08 has no answer for 624 rather than the 2010 statement.
expected.deletion_only_holding: No logical.holding_change row exists for the pair (372101, 353232), and it contributes to no account or customer position. No audit reports it as a violation: under the clause there was never a holding to withdraw, so its absence is the required behavior and an audit should hold that absence rather than tolerate it.
expected.everything_else: Account 428, its two statements plus the counterexample rollover statement, trades 353232 and 372101 with their attribution and outcomes, and the holding changes already derived from them are byte-identical to a run without this scenario. A withdrawal does not reach back through what already followed.
expected.reported_rows: inv.customer_withdrawal_with_standing_accounts_reported is expected to report one row per account that still has a standing statement at or after the withdrawal moment of the customer that owns it, naming the customer number, the account number, and the withdrawal moment. On this scenario the expected row count is ZERO and the reason matters: this document withdraws account 624, not its owner customer 238, and the invariant reports withdrawn customers with standing accounts. The row-producing case is a withdrawal of customer 238 while accounts 428 and 624 still stand, which would report two rows.

account_cdc.note: The withdrawal of account 624. A real CDC delete echoes the row's last values, so this one does too: ca_st_id ACTV and ca_tax_st 1 are 624's standing facts as of its 2010-02-07 statement. They are here precisely so that reading them is a visible error. The clause says a withdrawal creates nothing, so these values must not become a new statement, and must not restate the old one.

holding_history.note: A holding pair whose only report is a deletion, over two trades the brokerage already has. This is the case the positions Developer raised in questions_for_authority. The quantities are plausible and must not be used: the clause says there was never a holding here to withdraw.

observed: Measured on duckdb-native, and the reason matters more than the result. The withdrawal of account 624 is invisible -- 624 still carries its 2010-02-07 statement with is_current true and status ACTV, so an as-of question in 2018 answers with a statement the brokerage has withdrawn -- but not because ownership-history reads the flag and ignores it. ownership-history reads only raw.customer_mgmt_action; it never reads raw.account_cdc or raw.customer_cdc at all, because every one of its declared CDC handoffs is still deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time. So the account half of this counterexample cannot be exercised until that separate hole is answered, and no re-projection under L1.deletion-withdraws alone can discharge it. trade-lifecycle is the opposite case and the sharper one: valid_cdc_rows admits D, while only latest_outcome narrows to I and U, so a D-only trade today gets a persisted row with a placement, a frozen owner and a null outcome -- the direct opposite of a thing whose only reports are withdrawals having never been held. positions produces no holding_change for the deletion-only pair, which is the required outcome reached by the D row supplying no candidate quantity rather than by any rule, so nothing holds it.
tempting_wrong_repair: Three, in increasing subtlety. Physically deleting 624's rows, which erases history the clause says stands. Writing a 2017-07-08 statement for 624 whose standing facts are null, which leaves the record current with empty facts -- an answer where the clause says there is none. And filtering D rows out of the candidate set, which produces the right rows today and is still wrong, because it makes the withdrawal invisible: 624 keeps its 2010 statement as current and an as-of question in 2018 still answers with it.
why_constructed: L1.deletion-withdraws was accepted with no received record to exercise it: the TPC-DI fixture carries no D-flagged row in any source, so without a labeled constructed scenario the clause compiles untested and the three jobs can go on disagreeing about what a deletion means while every audit passes. Two cases, one per half of the clause. Account 624 is withdrawn after two real statements, which tests that earlier statements and earlier as-of answers stand while the record has no standing from the withdrawal forward. A holding pair reported only as a deletion tests the half the positions Developer actually asked about: a thing whose only reports are withdrawals was never held. Both use records the brokerage already has, per L1.constructed-scenarios: account 624 and trades 353232 and 372101 are all in the received data, and nothing here introduces a new one.
